description: The durable, source-stable provenance record for one occurrence (plan Sections 7.1, 7.4, and 7.5; STO-002, STO-010, STO-011; SID-005, SID-006). The server writes it as RFC 8785 canonical JSON at the deterministic occurrence key after the content-addressed blob is durable and before any upload attestation (plan Section 5, client data flow and server commit order). Every field is an input to, or a deterministic derivation of, the session, artifact, and occurrence identities, so the canonical bytes never vary by uploader or upload attempt (STO-010): uploader, request, transport, per-attempt authorization, and server commit material live in the upload attestation and the signed receipt, never here. The manifest is self-verifying — every derived value it carries (session_hash, artifact_hash, occurrence_id) is re-derivable from its own fields alone, so an auditor needs nothing but the object itself (STO-011). Unknown optional fields are retained and their semantics ignored (plan Section 7.1); the reserved names below are rejected outright because freezing uploader, request, transport, per-attempt, or server material in a source-stable record would break exactly the separation that keeps a relay from overwriting source provenance (SID-006; EC-05A; plan Section 3, decision on separate occurrence and attestation identity).

adapter_artifact_id.description: The adapter's opaque identifier for the source artifact; the last artifact-identity input (plan Section 7.4). The wire envelope is not durable, so without this field the artifact's identity would survive only as an unrecoverable hash input; storing it keeps the manifest sufficient to rebuild catalogs (STO-011).

adapter_build_id.description: Hypothetical v1.1 additive field pinned by the compatibility corpus: the adapter build that produced this projection. Provenance only; the artifact hash still binds exactly the v1 tuple.

adapter_id.description: The adapter that projected the artifact; an artifact-identity input (plan Section 7.4).

adapter_projection_version.description: Version of the adapter's projection (plan Section 7.1 adapter-projection version axis; STO-010 requires the adapter/projection version in the manifest). Preserved verbatim in provenance — a projection change is a different artifact, never a silent rewrite.

artifact_hash.description: H("artifact-v1", session_hash, artifact_kind, adapter_id, adapter_projection_version, adapter_artifact_id) per schemas/v1/ingest-identifiers.json (plan Section 7.4). Generation-stable by construction: replacement, truncation, or incompatible rewrite starts a fresh `generation` under the same artifact hash, preserving both histories (SID-003; EC-02).

artifact_kind.description: Kind of source artifact (plan Section 7.3): `file-slice` (exact complete-record byte slice) or `database-projection` (versioned allowlisted projection). An artifact-identity input, and the interpretive frame for the range coordinates below.

blob_digest.description: SHA-256 of the canonical uncompressed payload bytes — the one digest that names a blob (STO-001; plan Section 7.4). Several manifests may carry the same value: identical bytes under distinct session namespaces is one tenant-scoped blob plus distinct occurrences, which is deduplication working, not a conflict (STO-002; plan Section 3, same-bytes scenario). The stored blob's uncompressed size is recoverable from its `zstd-v1` frame header, so no size field is duplicated here.

generation.description: The source generation of this artifact snapshot (plan Sections 7.3 and 7.4): a UUIDv7 frozen when the generation was detected. An occurrence-identity input — a re-declared range under a new generation is a new occurrence, not an overwrite (SID-003).

harness.description: Harness identifier (plan Section 7.4 grammar). A session-identity input; the object key carries it as a validated opaque token.

id_source.description: Whether `upstream_session_id` was read from the harness (`upstream`) or adapter-minted for a missing harness session ID (`synthetic`, never inferred from a path name) — plan Section 7.4. Durably recorded so a synthetic ID is never later mistaken for harness-issued provenance.

occurrence_id.description: The manifest's own deterministic identity (plan Section 7.4; SID-005): H("occurrence-v1", session_hash, artifact_hash, generation, range_kind, range_start, range_end, blob_digest), constructed per schemas/v1/ingest-identifiers.json. Carried so the record is self-naming and re-derivable in place: an audit recomputes it from this manifest's own fields and refuses a mismatch (STO-011; VAL-005; PI-07 containment — fabrication creates new attributed objects, never corrupts archived ones).

occurrence_version.description: Occurrence-manifest schema major version (plan Section 7.1 version axis `occurrence_version`). Integer, currently 1; readers retain old-version support. New optional fields land inside v1; new required fields, redefined fields, a changed canonical field set, or changed identity rules require v2.

origin_client_id.description: The installation that captured the source (STO-010 requires origin in the manifest). Namespaces the logical session together with tenant, harness, and upstream session (SID-001); a relay uploader never replaces it with its own identity (ID-005; EC-05A) — who presented an upload is attestation material only.

range_end.description: Inclusive end coordinate of this chunk. Inside the occurrence identity (plan Section 7.4), so overlapping, gapped, split, or re-declared ranges produce distinct deterministic occurrences rather than corrupting one another (PI-05).

range_kind.description: Whether the coordinates below are byte offsets (`file-slice`) or projected-event ordinals (`database-projection`) — plan Section 7.4; SID-004's byte/event range and ordering information.

range_start.description: Inclusive start coordinate of this chunk in the generation's source stream (STO-010 source coordinates). Declared ranges are the uploader's assertion (PI-07); `range_start` at most `range_end` is server-side validation (VAL-002), not schema syntax.

session_hash.description: H("session-v1", tenant_id, origin_client_id, harness, upstream_session_id) per schemas/v1/ingest-identifiers.json (plan Section 7.4; SID-001). Namespaces the session — cloned harness UUIDs under a second origin client derive a distinct hash and never merge (SID-002; EC-03). Carried so catalogs group occurrences by logical session without re-deriving the hash from the wire envelope, which is not stored.

source_time.description: Optional UTC event time embedded in or derived from the source itself, when one exists (plan Section 7.5 canonical occurrence fields). Omitted — never null — when the source carries none. Source-stable and uploader-asserted (PI-07): it describes the source, not any upload of it.

storage_profile.description: The named canonical storage encoder of the blob this occurrence projects (plan Sections 7.5 and 7.6). Pins the stored form per occurrence so a later profile never rewrites the meaning of stored bytes under existing keys.

tenant_id.description: Issuer-created tenant identifier (plan Section 7.4). Scopes the object key and every derived identity below; cross-tenant writes are denied before any key is derived (SEC-003).

upstream_session_id.description: The harness's own session identifier, or the adapter-minted stand-in when `id_source` is `synthetic`, retained verbatim (SID-006: importers and mirrors preserve original provenance). Object keys hash it and never embed it (plan Section 7.5); the manifest, living in the encrypted/restricted raw namespace (SEC-002), keeps the original so the archive stays self-describing. Opaque UTF-8, never case-folded or Unicode-normalized.

title: Agent Archivist raw occurrence manifest (occurrence_version 1)

x-archivist.deduplication: STO-002: one manifest per distinct occurrence_id, including when several occurrences reference one blob
x-archivist.identityStability: STO-010: canonical fields MUST NOT vary by uploader or upload attempt — every field below is source-stable by construction, being an identity-hash input or a deterministic derivation of identity-hash inputs
x-archivist.writeOrder: after the blob is durable, before any upload attestation (plan Section 7.5; RCPT-001 ordering)
